title: Tiled attention: SIMD-friendly kernel with rope fusion and lazy-KV eviction heuristic
author: Alex Chen
description:
Motivation: reduce CPU/GPU stalls from strided attention and improve L2/SIMD utilization for medium-length contexts (128-2048). Prior work at Redwood uses fused rotary/rope transforms and FlashAttention variants; this change introduces a tiled attention kernel optimized for SIMT/SIMD packing, stitches in an in-kernel rope/rotary fusion path, and exposes a conservative lazy-KV eviction heuristic to reduce KV cache memory pressure under mixed-session workloads.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a tiled attention CUDA kernel that performs attention in 32x32 tiles with packed Q/K/V per lane and explicit prefetch of tiles into shared memory to improve throughput on Ampere+ GPUs. The kernel uses warp-level intrinsics to implement a fast softmax and supports fp16/qint8 code paths.
- Integrates rope/rotary fusion into the tiled kernel so position rotations are applied immediately after Q/K load, avoiding an extra memory pass for common rotary-based models.
- Introduces a lazy-KV eviction policy in runtime/kv/cache_manager.cpp. The policy evicts seldom-used KV shards only when the overall cache footprint exceeds a high watermark and prioritizes shards with longest time-since-last-access, preserving latency-sensitive prefixes.
- Small scheduler change: continuous-batching now detects tile-friendly payloads (multiple small sequences with similar lengths) and routes them to the tiled kernel via a new BatcherHint flag.
- Adds end-to-end perf tests and microbenchmarks (cpu/gpu) to validate improvements and regression-checks in CI.

Implementation notes: kernel is under runtime/ops/attn/tiling_kernel.cu with a driver wrapper runtime/ops/attn/tiling_entry.cpp. We kept the existing FlashAttention path as fallback for models that disable fused rotary or when kernel selection heuristics indicate better throughput for long-seq regimes. The tiled kernel supports quantized int8 paths via the existing QAT helpers. KV manager changes are conservative and guarded behind a runtime flag `--kv-eviction=lazy` to enable gradual rollout.

Performance: on T4/RTX6000/4090 matrix we saw:
- 128-token, batch=64: tiled kernel + rope fusion is ~1.6x faster than baseline FlashAttn v2 in our infra benchmarks.
- 512-token, batch=16: performance parity or slight regression (~0.95x) vs FlashAttn for very long sequences; scheduler keeps fallback path in that case.
- Memory: lazy-KV eviction reduced peak GPU KV cache memory by ~18% in mixed-session bench where many short-lived sessions were present.

Testing & safety: unit tests for correctness across rotary-enabled and disabled models added. Microbenchmarks included in tests/attn/perf/tiling_bench.py and a nightly bench that compares throughput and peak memory. CI initially failed on clang-tidy for a macro; fix was pushed in second commit and pipeline passed.

Rollout plan: merge to main -> canary on Dedicated GPUs with `--kv-eviction=lazy` disabled by default. After 2 weeks of canary, enable lazy eviction for workloads tagged `mixed-sessions` via per-customer config. Kernel selection is automatic but can be pinned per model via model config (runtime.model.attention_kernel = tiled|flash).

Related: ENG-987 (tiling-attn design doc), ENG-1012 (kv cache improvements). Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-987/tiling-attention-design and perf notes in docs/notes/tiling_attn.md.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel implementation + tests
- [x] KV manager heuristic + integration tests
- [x] Scheduler hint and routing tests
- [x] Benchmarks and CI green
- [x] Docs/notes updated

Notes for reviewers: focus on correctness of softmax numerics under fp16/qint8 paths, thread-safety of cache eviction, and scheduler hint API. The kernel includes debug paths to enable element-wise dumps for locally repro'ing mismatches.

review_comments: Maya Patel: Nice work overall. A few numeric nitpicks: can you add a fast-path test asserting stable softmax under adversarial large logits? Also please add an explicit check for rotary angle overflow in the fused path.
Alex Chen (author): Added stable-softmax test and guard for rotary angle in second commit; the guard snaps angles > 1e6 to modulo range to maintain FP16 stability.

Jordan Li: Thread-safety question on cache_manager: eviction touches the shard LRU metadata while reads may concurrently update last-access — we need to ensure we hold the shard-level mutex. Please add doc comments explaining the lock order to avoid deadlocks.
Alex Chen: Added mutex ordering docs and switched to shard-level try-lock to avoid head-of-line blocking during eviction. Added unit test that simulates concurrent access and evict.
Samir Gupta: Bench numbers look promising. Can you add a small note in docs that 512+ seqs still prefer FlashAttn and explain how to pin?
Alex Chen: Docs updated to show runtime.model.attention_kernel config and recommendation matrix.
release_notes: Introduce tiled SIMD-friendly attention kernel with in-kernel rope/rotary fusion and an opt-in lazy-KV eviction heuristic. Expected win for short-to-medium contexts and mixed-session workloads. Backwards compatible; FlashAttention remains available as a fallback.
